cards.text: Friend, the book of Matthew opens with a family tree. It's "the record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham." My family tree? A bin at a closing bakery and a 25-cent price sticker.

Then comes the list, father to son: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, down to David the king, down through the exile to Babylon, all the way to Joseph, the husband of Mary. A few moms make the list too, like Tamar, Rahab and Ruth. It adds up to three stretches of fourteen generations, and here I am losing count of the cookies on ONE tray.
Now here's how the birth of Jesus Christ came about. His mother Mary is pledged in marriage to Joseph, but they haven't come together yet.

cards.question: Before Mary and Joseph come together, Mary is found to be with child.
Mary is found to be with child before she and Joseph come together. Through whom?

cards.text: Joseph, her husband, is a righteous man. And he's unwilling to disgrace Mary publicly.

cards.question: Joseph is righteous and unwilling to disgrace Mary publicly. So what does he resolve to do?

cards.text: But after Joseph ponders these things, an angel of the Lord appears to him. Friend, the last time I heard of an angel dropping in on somebody, it was ME, in the back of a junk drawer, under a pile of takeout menus!

cards.question: After Joseph ponders all this, an angel of the Lord appears to him in a ___.

cards.text: And the angel starts with "Joseph, son of David." Hey, that family tree from the top of the book just showed up in one line!

cards.question: Joseph has resolved to divorce Mary quietly. The angel tells him to go ahead with it.

cards.text: Mary will give birth to a Son, the angel says, and Joseph is to give Him the name Jesus. No baby name book, no family group chat vote, the name comes SPECIAL DELIVERY!

cards.question: The angel says Joseph is to name Mary's Son Jesus. Why?

answers.text: He will save His people from their sins
He will rebuild the temple in Jerusalem
He will lead His people home from exile

cards.text: Then the book steps back: all this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet. The virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and they will call Him Immanuel.

cards.question: The prophet says they will call the Son Immanuel. What does the name Immanuel mean?
When Joseph wakes up, he does as the angel of the Lord commanded him and ___ Mary as his wife.
Joseph has no union with Mary until she gives birth to a Son.

cards.text: And when the Son is born, Joseph gives Him the name Jesus, just like the angel said. Trust me, friend, this story is barely out of the oven.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "the record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "Joseph, son of David.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question itself says Mary is with child before she and Joseph come together, which rules out the wrong answer "Joseph." That leaves a real choice between only two answers. Replace "Joseph" with another real Bible name that the setup doesn't rule out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The prophet is brought in only as "the prophet" and never identified. The prophecy comes from Isaiah (Isa 7:14). A fact from outside the passage is allowed with its reference, so the card could name Isaiah.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story-continues line opens with "Trust me, friend," which is lifted word for word from the doc's example line instead of being written fresh.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: The humor is thin, and after card 12 it stops entirely. Cards 3, 6, 10, 14 and 18 read as plain narration or mild pleasantness. Joseph's dilemma (card 6) and the prophecy (card 14) are moments that could carry a real laugh or reaction without muddying the facts. Card 10's line notices something but has no punchline.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
